name: Motorcycle
description: Every motor vehicle with a seat or saddle for the rider designed to travel on no more than three wheels, other than an electric bicycle. An electric two-wheeler past the motorized bicycle limits (2 brake horsepower, 30 mph, 32 inches wide, no shifting) is one. Defined by North Dakota Century Code §39-01-01 and regulated by chapter 39-10.2.

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle for the rider, and no more than three wheels on the ground
An electric two-wheeler with more than 2 brake horsepower (1,500 W), able to go faster than 30 mph, wider than 32 inches or needing the rider to shift, is a motorcycle rather than a motorized bicycle
Riders need a class M license or endorsement; the skill test can be waived for an approved motorcycle safety course

A class M learner's permit is available from 14, but at 14 and 15 only while enrolled in or after completing an approved safety course; it bars riding when headlights are required and carrying passengers
Riders under 16 must hold the permit for two months and complete the safety course before licensing, and may not ride a motorcycle over 510 cc
Riders and passengers under 18 must wear a safety helmet meeting US DOT standards, and a passenger must wear one whenever the operator must
Registered with the Department of Transportation, with one number plate
May not be ridden between lanes of traffic or more than two abreast in a lane
One built only for off-highway use is a class I off-highway vehicle instead
